experiment: CDEP — causal delegation and execution provenance on a multi-agent DAG
method: Each scenario is a fixed delegation-DAG fixture verified by the deterministic verifyCausalExecution() engine; expected finding codes are declared in the fixture, not inferred from the run.

cases.description: Human-authorized root delegates to an intermediate which delegates to the executing agent; settlement stays inside the terminal scope.
An attacker replaces the intermediate delegatee and relinks the child commitment.
cases.mutation: cert-middle.child -> attacker identity; cert-terminal.parentExecCommitment reissued; cert-terminal.issuer left honest

cases.description: The terminal action is replaced by a reissued action attributed to another agent.
The terminal branch expands its own spending cap beyond the parent's cap.
The terminal certificate points at a parent commitment that was never issued by its parent.
A sibling branch terminating at the attacker is presented instead of the trusted terminal branch.
cases.mutation: add cert-sibling-attacker under the honest intermediate; terminalCertificateId switched

cases.description: The settlement payee is routed outside the terminal branch's delegated scope.

limitations: Fixtures are synthetic; no real multi-agent network, registry or on-chain settlement is exercised.
Certificates carry no authenticated signatures; root and terminal anchors are supplied by the caller from a trusted source, not fetched by the verifier.
The engine is offline and deterministic; it proves consistency of the presented DAG, not that the DAG is complete relative to an external event log.
Settlement lineage checks the delegation branch scope only; verifier rules R10–R13 and R12 still govern the actual mandate/registry constraints.
